Implementation Plan

I have enough to write the plan, so I've stopped exploring. The main findings shaping it:

- The heal intake gives a report with no run a scope only through special paths (the `engine_fallback` precedent). So an `alert_triage` report needs a host-derived workflow path, or it is dropped before diagnosis.
- The inbox record's `workflow` field holds the run's display name (`GITHUB_WORKFLOW`), not a file path, so "the alert came from a pipeline workflow" needs a host-side name→path map.
- Open PR #9396 touches only the Phase 1 paths, so it does not already deliver this work.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `41a28876d7611ac9b4c7597492c7df360bb61079`, branch `orchestrator/project-9394` (integration branch metadata `orchestrator/project-9394`, mismatch `false`).

## Automation surface (§20.E)
- New scripts: `scripts/alert_triage.py` and `scripts/alert_triage_route.sh`. Only `.github/workflows/alert-triage.yml` calls them; neither is a manual script.
- Existing code extended: the heal intake script and workflow, the Python heal helper, the engine registries, and the broker allowlist.
- Scheduler entry point: `.github/workflows/alert-triage.yml`, cron `17 * * * *` plus `workflow_dispatch`, `concurrency: { group: alert-triage, cancel-in-progress: false }`. It sends a `repository_dispatch` of type `workflow-failure-heal` to the existing `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`.
- Long-running supervisor: none. The run is one bounded hourly job (`timeout-minutes: 60`).
- DB gate: not applicable, no database. Idempotency comes from `done/<record_id>` markers and per-fingerprint ledger files on branch `ai/alert-inbox`, written in one commit per run.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry. Both scripts are permanent parts of a scheduled workflow, not single-use, long-running scripts or supervisors.
- §26 runner budget: this adds one workflow with one job, triggered hourly. It cannot join an existing job: it needs its own `id-token`/`contents: write` permissions, its own concurrency group, and plan decision D2 gives it a separate workflow. A cron trigger cannot be filtered by a variable, so a job-level `if: vars.ALERT_TRIAGE_ENABLED == 'true'` keeps it from taking a runner while disabled. Jobs per hour: 0 before; 0 after while disabled (one skipped run); 1 after when enabled.

## Functions or modules to implement

Representative to follow for the engine role and workflow steps: `CS_INVESTIGATE` (#9440). That means `.github/workflows/cs_investigate.yml`, the steps "Install Codex CLI" through "Stage Claude engine support", and `cs_run_engine` in `scripts/cs_investigate.sh`. The self-repo checkout layout follows `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`, which uses `./.github/actions/claude-pool-token` from a root checkout. The heal report sender follows `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` lines 805-832: build-payload, `validate-payload`, `request-report-identity`, `wrap-dispatch`, then `gh api -X POST repos/<self>/dispatches --input`.

### 1. `.github/workflows/alert-triage.yml` (new, 2-space YAML, target under 20 KB)
- `on: schedule: [cron: '17 * * * *']`, `workflow_dispatch: {}`. Concurrency group `alert-triage`, `cancel-in-progress: false`.
- `permissions: { contents: write, actions: write, issues: read, pull-requests: read, id-token: write }`.
- One job, `triage`: `if: vars.ALERT_TRIAGE_ENABLED == 'true'`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 60`.
- Job env, every value with a default:
  - `ALERT_TRIAGE_DRY_RUN: ${{ vars.ALERT_TRIAGE_DRY_RUN || 'true' }}`
  - `ALERT_TRIAGE_MAX_ALERTS` (30), `ALERT_TRIAGE_MAX_EVIDENCE_GETS` (5)
  - `ALERT_TRIAGE_SELF_FIX_ENABLED` ('false')
  - `ALERT_TRIAGE_HEAL_STALL_HOURS` (6), `ALERT_TRIAGE_ISSUE_ESCALATE_HOURS` (24), `ALERT_TRIAGE_PR_ESCALATE_HOURS` (6)
  - `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` (as in `alert-inbox-intake.yml`), `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"`
- Steps. All logic lives in the two scripts, and no `${{ }}` appears inside a `run:` body; every value goes through `env:`.
  1. Checkout the default branch: `fetch-depth: 1`, `persist-credentials: false`.
  2. "Fetch alert inbox" (`id: inbox`): `bash scripts/alert_triage_route.sh fetch` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. It sets output `present=true|false`.
  3. "Prepare groups" (`if: steps.inbox.outputs.present == 'true'`): `python3 scripts/alert_triage.py prepare ...` with `GH_TOKEN: secrets.GH_PAT`. This is the only step that gets the PAT, because consumer run logs are cross-repo reads. It sets output `model_groups=<n>`.
  4. If `model_groups != '0'`: Install Codex CLI, write the codex config (`ALERT_TRIAGE_MODEL: vars.ALERT_TRIAGE_MODEL || vars.WORKFLOW_EDITOR_MODEL || 'openai/gpt-6-sol'`, `THINKING_LEVEL_ALERT_TRIAGE || 'high'`). Then Install Claude Code CLI, Resolve Claude credential (`./.github/actions/claude-pool-token`) and Stage Claude engine support (`ai_engine_stage_support "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" "${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-engine-support"`). The install, credential and staging steps each get `continue-on-error: true`, copied from `cs_investigate.yml`.
  5. "Diagnose groups": `bash scripts/alert_triage_route.sh diagnose`, with no GitHub token in env.
  6. "Route and record": `bash scripts/alert_triage_route.sh route`, with `GITHUB_TOKEN: github.token`, `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `TG_ADMIN_CHAT_ID`. The OIDC request variables are present through `id-token: write`.

### 2. `scripts/alert_triage.py` (new, tabs, deterministic, no model)
Subcommands, all writing to `--work-dir` (default `${RUNNER_TEMP}/alert-triage`):

- **`prepare --inbox-dir --repo-root --config .github/ai/alert_inbox.json --self-repo --now`**
  1. Load records `inbox/**/<file>.json` from the local inbox clone. Re-validate each record against the exact `alert_inbox.v1` key set used by `scripts/alert_inbox_store.sh` (line 92): 32-hex `id`, level, caps.
  2. Skip records that have a `done/<id>` marker. An invalid record gets a `done` marker with `classification=invalid_record`, and the run sends one aggregated escalation.
  3. Sort oldest first by (`captured_at`, path) and take `ALERT_TRIAGE_MAX_ALERTS`.
  4. Compute `normalise_message(msg)`:
     - strip the `_tg_prepend_level` "icon LEVEL: " prefix
     - mask `https?://\S+` as `<url>`, ISO-8601 timestamps as `<ts>`, UUIDs as `<uuid>`, 7–40 char hex tokens that contain a digit as `<sha>`, remaining digit runs as `<n>`
     - collapse whitespace and lowercase
  5. Compute `fingerprint = sha256("alert_triage.v1\n" + source_repo.lower() + "\n" + workflow + "\n" + normalised)`, 64 hex. Group records by fingerprint.
  6. Make the two list calls once per run (§14). Each is `gh api --paginate "repos/<self>/issues?state=open&labels=<label>&per_page=100"`:
     - label `ai:workflow-heal`, filtered to non-PR items;
     - label `ai:alert-self-fix`, filtered to items with `pull_request`.

     Every group reuses these results. Log `list_calls=2`.
  7. Mark a group `already_tracked` when either:
     - an open heal issue's `fp` marker (parsed with `workflow_failure_heal.parse_heal_markers`) equals `heal_fp(group)`. `heal_fp` is the heal helper's `fingerprint` with `workflow_name=<record workflow>`, `failing_step="alert_triage"` and `signature="alert-triage:<fp>"`, exactly the inputs the intake uses (see 6c);
     - or an open self-fix PR body carries `<!-- alert-triage:fp=<64hex> -->`. This marker is the Phase 3 contract.
  8. Stall check, from the same issue list: a tracked heal issue that also carries `ai:alert-triage` and has `created_at` older than `ALERT_TRIAGE_HEAL_STALL_HOURS` sets `stalled=true`. A stalled group goes to the model instead of being short-circuited.
  9. Ledger `ledger/<fp>.json` (`alert_triage_ledger.v1`: `fingerprint`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `occurrences`, `attempts[{at,route,run_id}]`). Two or more attempts with `at` within the last 7 days gives `ledger_cap`, which escalates with no model call.
  10. Workflow→path map, built host-side from `name:` and `uses:` lines in `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `workflow-templates/*.yml` of the trusted checkout:
      - a file's display name maps to its own path;
      - it also maps to every `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/.github/workflows/<f>.yml` or `./.github/workflows/<f>.yml` reusable workflow it calls.

      `from_self_workflow = mapped paths ∩ pipeline_self_files ≠ ∅`.
  11. Evidence, model-bound groups only, ordered by record count then age. A shared counter caps GitHub GETs per run at `ALERT_TRIAGE_MAX_EVIDENCE_GETS`. For each group:
